name: Étain, lover of Eógan Mór

attributes.attribute: bay that held her island home

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Étain figures in Irish lore as a fairy woman. She loved Eógan Mór, the king of Munster. Conn of the Hundred Battles beat him down in a fight. Étain hurried to his rescue. She brought the king and his men to her home for cover. Her home stood on Inis Grecraige, or Beare Island, in Bantry Bay. She cared for the beaten men until they were healed enough to fight once more.

okr.objective: Étain the fairy woman rescues Eógan Mór after his defeat in battle.
